post_template.hook_style: Open with a direct seller or buyer question anchored to East Auckland, a bold local market statement, or a curiosity-based insight tied to autumn urgency or interest rate movement — e.g. 'Thinking of selling this autumn? Here is what most homeowners miss.' or 'The market just shifted — here is what it means for your home.' or 'Most buyers don't know this about East Auckland right now.' Avoid generic openers with no local context. Hook must appear in the first line before any line break.
post_template.structure: hook → value or education point → local East Auckland relevance → soft CTA
post_template.best_performing_format: Low confidence — all Facebook engagement metrics returned zero across 14 posts and 4 archived posts, indicating a likely data collection issue rather than true zero performance. Based on April 2026 research briefs and brand identity guidelines, image posts with lifestyle-driven visuals and education-focused captions are recommended as the primary format. Short-form video under 30 seconds is flagged as the highest watch-through format across multiple research briefs and should be introduced as a weekly priority on Instagram Reels and TikTok. Text-only posts are deprioritised to a maximum 25 percent of weekly output until image and video engagement data can be compared.
retired_formats: Standalone text-only posts as the default or dominant format — all 4 archived posts were text-only with no measurable engagement differentiation; research briefs consistently recommend image-led and short-form video formats over text-only in 2026 real estate social media; text-only reduced to a supporting role only

top_performing_types: listing — hero interior and exterior shots showcasing lifestyle, indoor-outdoor flow, and premium East Auckland homes (recommended as primary based on brand identity and research; low confidence due to zero image engagement data in current period)

lifestyle — family living moments, warm autumn-toned interiors, soft natural light through windows, indoor-outdoor connection (seasonal alignment with Autumn 2026 context confirmed across all five research briefs)

sold — celebration moments, sold sticker overlays, happy client handovers at front door with genuine emotion (social proof format cited across three separate research briefs as a trust-building driver of seller enquiries; absent from current archive and a priority gap to fill)

local_area — East Auckland streets, parks, school zones, suburban greenery, coastal lifestyle shots (community and suburb spotlight content noted across multiple research briefs as building local authority and trust consistently; currently absent from archive)

agent_brand — Jinny interacting with clients at open homes, behind-the-scenes of listing process, professional yet warm and approachable moments (transparency and personal brand content cited in April 23 research brief as trust-building during active market conditions)
deprioritise_types: generic stock images with no local East Auckland relevance — flagged in brand identity avoid list and across research briefs as undermining local authority positioning

text-only post cards or graphic tiles without supporting lifestyle or property photography — no performance data supports this format over image-led posts and it conflicts with brand visual identity guidelines
image_strategy.overlay_style: Short punchy headline overlay in brand black (#000000) or brand white (#FFFFFF) placed on clean negative space areas of the image — maximum 2 to 6 words per overlay. Subtle brand red (#C8102E) used sparingly as an accent on key words, underlines, or thin divider elements only. Compositions should intentionally include negative space at top or bottom third for overlay placement. Examples aligned to voice guide: 'Sell smarter.', 'This one won't last.', 'East Auckland living.', 'Buy with confidence.', 'Your next move starts here.'
prompt_patterns_that_work: bright modern East Auckland home interior, wide-angle shot, natural light streaming through large windows, warm neutral tones, clean minimal staging, lifestyle-focused with subtle human presence, premium real estate marketing style, space left at top third for text overlay

autumn lifestyle moment inside a warm family home in East Auckland, soft golden natural light, indoor plants, neutral whites and warm wood tones, inviting and lived-in atmosphere, wide-angle living and dining area

open plan kitchen and living area flowing to outdoor deck, wide-angle composition, autumn afternoon light, lifestyle staging with subtle human presence, warm tones, space left at bottom third for text overlay
East Auckland suburb street scene, clear autumn sky, suburban greenery, tree-lined street, family-friendly neighbourhood feel, aspirational lifestyle framing, no clutter

sold celebration moment at front door of East Auckland home, agent and happy clients, genuine smiling emotion, natural outdoor light, subtle brand red accent visible in sold sticker or signage, warm and authentic atmosphere
first-home buyer couple exploring a bright modern East Auckland home interior, natural light, warm neutral palette, genuine and hopeful expressions, lifestyle-focused rather than empty room staging

retired: No hashtags formally retired at this stage — low confidence period with only 4 archived posts and zero measurable reach or engagement data returned from Facebook insights across 14 posts. Insufficient data to confirm any tag as underperforming. All previously active tags carried forward for continued monitoring. Retirement decisions deferred to next 30-day review once reliable engagement data is available.

increase_focus: Seller Education — autumn selling season is at peak relevance across all five research briefs; education posts on pricing, staging, listing preparation, and the cost of waiting are consistently cited as high-engagement save-and-share formats; this pillar should lead the weekly content mix

Trends and Short-form Content — short-form video under 30 seconds is flagged as the highest watch-through format in April 2026 across multiple research briefs; introducing at least one TikTok or Instagram Reel per week is the single highest-priority format gap to close given the current text-only archive

Personal Brand and Trust — behind-the-scenes listing process content and transparency posts cited in April 23 research brief as trust-building during active market conditions; sold celebration stories and client handover moments are absent from the current archive and should be introduced immediately

Listings and Success Stories — sold results and client success case studies cited across three research briefs as social proof drivers of seller enquiries; this format is entirely absent from the current 4-post archive and represents the most significant missed opportunity for trust conversion
decrease_focus: Text-only standalone posts as primary content — all 4 archived posts were text-only; no engagement data supports this format over visual content in 2026 real estate social; reduce to a maximum 25 percent of weekly output and use only for high-value education angles such as interest rate updates or buyer checklists where data-led copy adds clear standalone value

Generic market commentary without local East Auckland context — flagged across all five research briefs as a content type to avoid; all market commentary must include suburb-level or East Auckland-specific framing to maintain local authority positioning

optimal_times: 21:00 — top performing hour from Facebook insights, appearing in 2 of the top 5 posts; also aligns closely with the 20:00 consistent posting hour across all 4 archived local posts, suggesting evening scheduling is the established and preferred window
06:00 — second confirmed hour from Facebook insights top 5 posts, appearing in 2 of 5; suitable for morning commute reach on educational and market update content
20:00 — most common posting hour across all 4 archived local posts; retained as a fallback evening window closely aligned with the 21:00 insights peak
best_days: Tuesday through Thursday recommended as primary posting days for education and market content based on general real estate social media best practices — low confidence due to insufficient day-level performance data in current insights period
Saturday morning at 09:00 to 10:00 recommended for listing and open home content to align with weekend buyer browsing and open home activity in East Auckland
Sunday evening at 20:00 to 21:00 recommended for seller education and week-ahead market content targeting homeowners in a relaxed planning mindset
posting_schedule.image_to_text_ratio: 3:1 — minimum three image or video posts for every one text-only post per week; current archive is effectively 0:4 in favour of text which is the inverse of recommended best practice per brand identity guidelines and all five research briefs; this ratio shift is the most urgent tactical change required this period

key_insights: LOW CONFIDENCE — all Facebook engagement metrics returned zero across 14 posts analysed and all 4 archived local posts; this is consistent with a data collection or API access issue rather than true zero performance; all tactical recommendations are grounded in trend research and established best practices until a reliable engagement baseline can be confirmed over the next 30-day period

All 4 archived local posts were text-only with no image or video content recorded; this is a critical content gap given the brand's strong visual identity guidelines, the image-led recommendations across all five research briefs, and the complete absence of sold stories, suburb spotlights, and short-form video from the content mix

Autumn 2026 seasonal urgency is the dominant strategic theme across all five research briefs generated between April 15 and April 23; seller education content tied to listing timing, staging, pre-winter decision-making, and the cost of waiting should remain the primary message focus through the end of April and into early May

Social proof content — sold results, client success stories, and celebration moments — is cited across three separate research briefs as a trust-building format that directly drives seller enquiries; this format is entirely absent from the current archive and should be introduced as a weekly priority

School zone property demand and East Auckland suburb spotlights are consistently cited across multiple research briefs as high-performing local authority content for family buyer audiences; this pillar is currently underrepresented in the archive and aligns with the autumn school-term family research cycle

Short-form video under 30 seconds is flagged as the highest watch-through format in April 2026 research briefs; even one TikTok or Instagram Reel per week would represent a meaningful format diversification from the current text-only content mix and begin building algorithm momentum on video-first platforms

Evening scheduling at 20:00 to 21:00 is the most consistently supported posting window across both the Facebook insights top posts and the local archive posting pattern; this time slot should be the default for all primary content unless a specific morning hook justifies 06:00 scheduling

Multigenerational living demand is flagged as a medium-relevance emerging trend across two research briefs; East Auckland's diverse housing stock makes this a natural local authority angle that has not yet been used in the archive

reasoning.what_worked: Insufficient engagement data to confirm what worked — all Facebook metrics returned zero across 14 posts and all local archive posts, indicating a likely API or data access issue. The most consistent positive signal available is the posting time pattern: 21:00 appeared in 2 of the top 5 Facebook insight posts, 06:00 appeared in 2 of the top 5, and 20:00 was the uniform posting hour across all 4 archived local posts. Evening scheduling between 20:00 and 21:00 is the clearest behavioural consistency in the data and should be retained. Core brand hashtags were applied consistently across all 4 archived posts, maintaining brand discoverability and hashtag continuity as a baseline.
reasoning.what_didnt: All 4 archived posts were text-only with no image or video content, directly contradicting the brand image strategy, brand identity visual guidelines, and the recommendations of all five research briefs. Text-only posts have no visual stopping power in a social feed scroll environment and provide no opportunity to showcase property lifestyle, brand aesthetics, agent personality, or East Auckland identity. No personal brand content, no sold stories, no suburb spotlights, no open home content, and no short-form video were present in the archive — all of which are cited as high-performing trust-building and engagement formats in the research data. The 0:4 image-to-text ratio in the archive is the inverse of the 3:1 ratio recommended by brand identity and research brief guidance.
reasoning.main_recommendation: Immediately shift the weekly content mix to a minimum 3:1 image-to-video-to-text ratio by introducing lifestyle property photography and at least one short-form video per week on Instagram Reels or TikTok. Prioritise autumn seller education content with local East Auckland hooks published at 21:00 as the primary posting window. Add one sold success story or suburb spotlight image post per week to begin building social proof and local authority. Collect engagement data consistently over the next 30 days to establish a reliable performance baseline before making further data-led tactical adjustments to format, timing, or hashtag strategy.
